subject: Clarify billing for partial streaming sessions, disconnects & retries
messages:
From: Oliver Park <oliver.park@healthbyte.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T16:03:00-05:00
Subject: Billing for partial streaming outputs and retry behavior

Ben —

Quick question as we're mapping out the integration costs for our real-time summarization flow: how does Redwood bill in these edge cases for streaming responses? Specifically:

- If a client starts a streaming generation and disconnects after a few tokens (partial generation), do we get charged for the tokens that were generated but never fully delivered?
- If the client reconnects and triggers a retry for the same user session, do you treat it as a continuation (no new charge) or a new billable generation?
- What about server-side retries (timeouts on your side) that resend tokens — are those deduplicated for billing?

I attached a small sample session log from our side (HealthByte_sample_session_log.csv) to show our pattern — lots of short sessions with occasional reconnects. We're trying to estimate monthly spend and whether to pursue a committed discount.

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver Park
Head of Platform Engineering, HealthByte Labs
oliver.park@healthbyte.com

Attachment: HealthByte_sample_session_log.csv (CSV, 12KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@healthbyte.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T18:22:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Billing for partial streaming outputs and retry behavior

Oliver —

Thanks for the log, that helps. Short answers up-front, then some clarifying detail:

- We bill for tokens that the runtime successfully emits server-side. If a token generation completes on our side and is included in the server-to-client output stream, it is counted.
- For disconnects + client-initiated reconnects, we try to detect session continuations (same session id + KV cache reuse). If the reconnect happens within the defined grace window and can resume from the same KV cache, we treat it as a continuation and avoid double-billing for already-emitted tokens.
- Server-side retries that are idempotent (re-emitting the same token sequence due to transient infra retries) are deduplicated by our metering layer where possible; if a retry legitimately produces new tokens those are billable.

Couple of clarifying Qs for our billing team: the sample shows many disconnects under 10s and some reconnects after 45–90s. Can you confirm how often you expect reconnects within 30s vs >60s? That will affect whether we can declare them as the same session.

I attached our public rate card for reference and looped Marissa for discount/commit question.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Priya Rao <priya.raoprocur@healthbyte.com>

Cc: Oliver Park <oliver.park@healthbyte.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Billing for partial streaming outputs and retry behavior

Ben —

Forwarding to add our procurement lens. Two procurement-specific asks:

1) When you say "grace window" can you commit to a numeric value we can put in contract language (30s/60s)?
2) If we purchase committed throughput (dedicated or reserved capacity), do partial-disconnects still count against the commit in the same way? Would we get credits back for sessions where no token was produced (e.g., client closed pre-first-token)?

We will need exact wording for the SOW so our legal team can review.

Thanks,
Priya Rao
Senior Procurement Manager, HealthByte Labs
priya.raoprocur@healthbyte.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya.raoprocur@healthbyte.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Oliver Park <oliver.park@healthbyte.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Billing for partial streaming outputs and retry behavior

Hi Priya / Oliver —

We can absolutely provide contract-friendly language. High level our proposals for HealthByte given the observed pattern:

- Grace window: 30 seconds by default. If a reconnect with the same session id and cache reuse occurs within 30s, we treat it as the same generation for billing purposes (no duplicate charge). We can extend to 60s for committed capacity customers as a negotiated term.

- Partial generations: only server-emitted tokens count. If the client connects and then closes before any tokens are emitted, that session is non-billable. If at least one token is emitted server-side, it is billable. For clarity we will include an example calculation in the SOW.

- Server retries: our metering layer deduplicates retries that re-emit identical token sequences within the same request window. Non-idempotent retries that produce additional tokens are billable.

- Committed capacity: for customers on reserved capacity we can offer a monthly credit buffer (e.g., the first N short sessions per 10k sessions not counted toward the commit) or a small monthly PRORATION model to smooth short-session noise. We can propose two tiers: a conservative buffer (1% of monthly usage) or a generous buffer (3%) depending on contract level.

Ben — I recommend we propose the 30s standard + 60s for Dedicated commit and include a line-item for a monthly short-session buffer in the SOW draft. I can handle the discount language once Ben confirms expected ARR/commit size. 

Oliver — attaching a short draft SOW and our rate card link. If you like, we can put a formal clause in the SOW that enumerates exactly: grace window, what counts as an emitted token, server-retry dedup rules, and the buffer percent for committed customers.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya.raoprocur@healthbyte.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Oliver Park <oliver.park@healthbyte.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T11:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Billing for partial streaming outputs and retry behavior — billing model details

Thanks all — adding final billing specifics from the metering/billing side you can reference in the SOW. We'll include these as explicit contract terms so procurement/legal have clear language. Summary rules: 

1) Metering unit: billable token = token successfully produced by the inference runtime. For streaming APIs this maps to the token sequences our runtime acknowledged as emitted.

2) Partial deliveries: if the runtime produced >=1 token, that token count is billable. If a session terminates before any token emission, it will not appear on the invoice.

3) Grace window & session continuation: default grace window = 30s. If a reconnect within 30s reuses the same internal session id and resumes from the same KV cache, we treat the reconnect as continuation and mark previously-emitted tokens as already-metered. For Dedicated/Committed customers we can extend the window to 60s by agreement.

4) Retries/deduplication: our metering layer assigns a request fingerprint. Retries that re-emit identical token sequences within a 2-minute reconciliation window are deduplicated and only counted once. Retries that generate additional tokens are billed for the delta. Note: if you intentionally trigger application-level retries that cause duplicate distinct requests, those are billable unless the fingerprint and cache heuristics coalesce them.

5) Invoice presentation & credits: invoices show line items for total streamed tokens and a note for any short-session buffer applied. For committed customers we apply the agreed buffer/credit automatically each billing period. For one-off credits (e.g., an incident where our infra retransmitted tokens) we can issue manual credits upon review.

6) Example (from your sample): if a session emitted 12 tokens then the client disconnected and reconnected after 20s and resumed with +8 tokens, invoice shows 20 tokens. If disconnected after 12 tokens and never reconnected, invoice shows 12 tokens. If session closed pre-first-token, invoice shows 0 for that session.

Next steps: Marissa — please confirm the buffer % you want to propose (1% vs 3%) and target commit ARR so we can prepare a final SOW. Priya / Oliver — let us know whether 30s default + 60s for commit works for you; we can reflect it in the SOW and in HubSpot deal HLB-2026-087.

-Karthik
